title: What Is UX
summary: UX is the quality of the complete journey: usefulness, usability, accessibility, trust and context—not visual polish alone.

MUST.text: Define user, task, context and success outcome before proposing screens.
Map discovery, entry, task completion, recovery and post-task touchpoints.
Separate observed evidence from assumptions and name a validation method.

SHOULD.text: Measure task success, time, errors and confidence together.
Include policy, data, support and device constraints.

AVOID.text: Treat stakeholder preference or visual polish as usability evidence.
Invent personas, quotes or conversion metrics.

DECIDE.decision: Label each and name a validation method

DECIDE.situation: Journey has a gap (discovery, recovery, post-task)
DECIDE.decision: Map and improve the full path

FAILURE_MODES: A polished screen can still fail the task; validate against the defined user outcome.
Optimizing one touchpoint while ignoring discovery or recovery leaves the end-to-end journey broken.
Personas or metrics invented without evidence produce decisions that do not match real users.

sources.title: Nielsen Norman Group — The Definition of User Experience (UX)
ISO 9241-210:2019 Human-centred design for interactive systems
